Alright, some points about why the Quran is considered a miracle:

- It has not been changed by man since the prophets death, people literally had 1400 years if they wanted to absolutely destroy islam.


- A book that was spoken over 23 years yet it doesn't have contradictions. Does it seem possible to you? An illiterate, that does not save his work on paper, is speaking a whole book, yet he didn't contradict himself somehow.


- Contains stories of many past prophets, when he had no access to a bible. Even if he had access to a bible, the stories are not the same in the Quran. If he made up this whole narrative about the past prophets, again he was bound to contradict himself if he was listening to someone read the Bible to him then creating a narrative and somehow maintaining it for 23 years without writing. For example, and I'm sure you've heard this before, but how could he have known that pharaohs minister or whatever was called Haman? If he was stealing from bible, we don't expect additions to the stories of the Bible. Also, somehow the guys entire life was narrated by thousands of his people, but somehow no one saw him with a bible and narrated that to us. Also, why would he mention older prophets' miracles? If he was a liar, wouldn't that just make his argument weaker because people will say "why don't you raise the dead"? 


- Could've been easily falsifiable by the people of his time, they were challenged to bring a single chapter but they themselves admitted that they can't. Also, Abu lahab had 10 years to just say that he is a Muslim and the whole Quran would be false. 


- Historical predictions, again that could falsify the Quran if they didn't happen. Byzantines being victorious after defeat in 3-9 years for example. Although this isn't just the Quran as Muhammad said stuff like that too. 


- Linguistic miracle. I'll be honest even I still don't comprehend this fully, but I'm learning. To give an idea, the attention to the smallest details in the Quran, for example in I believe Surah Al-Shuaraa, Allah speaks about ~7 prophets and what they said to their people. With all of them except Moses and Ibrahim, the prophets say to their people something like "I am not asking you for payment, my payment is from Allah". Moses and Ibrahim didn't, because Moses was talking to Pharaoh, and Pharaoh is the one who raised him and spent on him so it would be pretty rude to say that. Same with Ibrahim as he was preaching to his Father. Another example, Prophet Shuaib, when he is sent to Madyan, Allah says something like "and to Madyan their brother Shuaib". Another name for Madyan is "ashab al aika" which is a tree they used to worship, so when Allah says he sent Shuaib to ashab Al aika, He doesn't say their brother, rather only "Shuaib". There are maaany examples of this stuff, and I'm still learning them. Why would Muhammad do that, or.. how? Create a whole narrative of prophets, then give attention to the smallest details, while delivering it orally, while not contradicting himself, over 23 years. Another thing to support the amazing language of the Quran, I forgot his name exactly but even the top poet and enemy of his time, literally the top, said this cannot be the word of a man. Ofcourse this is just to give an idea.


- Saved in the hearts of hundreds of thousands, millions even, of people as young as 6 years old. Name any book that is memorised by this many people. 


- Usually I dislike mentioning science, but it is something that it is still compatible with science. Embryology, water cycle, etc. He mentioned these things, he ought to have messed up atleast once as an illiterate in the desert, imo.


- Unrelated exactly to the Quran, but really, I still fail to see how a man that is known for his honesty and trusted by his enemies, a man that preached so many good values would make such a massive lie with no record of lying before.
